messages:
maya: heads up — during the canary run for model-redwood-3-quant we got a p95 latency spike at about concurrency=48. baseline (redwood-3-fp16) was fine. logs below.

maya: snippet from runner logs:
```
[2026-03-20T14:12:03Z] runner: enqueue ok, batch_size=16, kvcache_hit=0
[2026-03-20T14:12:03Z] gpu0: kernel_select: int8_path enabled
[2026-03-20T14:12:04Z] runner: backpressure: fanout_queue len=120, worker_busy=95%
[2026-03-20T14:12:04Z] perf: p95=842ms, p50=98ms
```

lee: :thinking: interesting. so p50 unchanged but tail massively worse — sounds like queuing/backpressure or a pathological batching window. which runner flags did you use?

maya: used the eval harness default flags: `--concurrency=48 --batch-window-ms=10 --prefetch=2` and quant profile `int8/actq` from the catalog.

arjun: did you test with `--continuous-batching=false`? that can change ordering and avoid very large batches when concurrency jumps. also check `--max-batch=32`.

samira: pinging perf-bot to re-run a controlled sweep (concurrency 8,16,32,48,64) and capture batch size distribution + kvcache hit rate. can we get cost/token too?

perf-bot: scheduled job 1851123456-1 started. running sweep: conc=[8,16,32,48,64], duration=5m per step. results will be uploaded to https://redwood.internal/dashboards/evals/1851123456

lee: quick hypothesis: int8 quant path increases per-token kernel latency slightly, but if kvcache prefetch displacement occurs under heavy fanout we might re-stream more KV loads. that plus larger batches could blow p95. check `kv_prefetch_limit` and `kv_cache_ttl` values in the canary config.

maya: config shows `kv_prefetch_limit=4`, `kv_cache_ttl_s=900`. I'll try bumping prefetch to 8 and reducing batch-window to 4ms to see if tail improves.

arjun: also make sure the runner ordering patch (PR #462) is deployed to the canary nodes — previous CI runs had off-by-one where empty-batches were emitted. that produced occasional 500ms stalls.

maya: confirmed PR #462 is on canary. not sure it's active in this container image; I'll rebase the harness image and re-run.

perf-bot: step conc=48 finished. metrics: p95=810ms, p50=104ms, avg_batch_size=28, kvcache_hit=12%. attaching sample trace id 0x7b9f.

samira: those kvcache_hit numbers are low. baseline model had ~58% hit at same workload. did the quant build alter prefix keys? maybe tokenization mismatch?

lee: good call — quant-aware tokenization change happened in the tokenizer refactor. that could change cache key normalization. run `diff-tokenizer-keys` on a sample.

maya: running diff locally, 23/1000 examples show different keys (trailing-space normalization bug). opening issue.

arjun: while that gets fixed, we should update the eval dashboard and CI alerting: set alert for p95 > 600ms for canary evals covering quantized models, and create a metric that tracks kvcache_hit delta vs baseline model per-run.

samira: agreed. creating dashboard tile: "p95_delta_vs_baseline" and a derived metric "kvcache_hit_delta". also add a CI gating rule: if p95_delta > 200ms OR kvcache_hit_delta < -20% fail the canary.

maya: will also add a short runnable repro script to the eval harness repo: `scripts/repro_concurrency.sh` with the exact flags. pasting snippet:
```bash
./run_eval --model model-redwood-3-quant --concurrency $1 --batch-window-ms $2 --duration 300
```

perf-bot: repro job queued. note: cost-per-token for quant run is slightly lower (0.72x) but tail degradation might offset savings for latency-sensitive routes.

lee: we should add a column to the rollout dashboard that shows effective cost-per-successful-request = cost_per_token * (1 + tail_penalty_factor). that helps PMs weigh tradeoffs.

samira: i'll add the column and wire it to the rollout policy UI so a canary can auto-fail for high effective cost.

maya: thanks. action items: 1) maya fix tokenizer key bug (on it) 2) maya re-run sweep with batch-window=4ms and prefetch=8 3) samira add dashboard tiles + CI gating 4) arjun verify runner ordering on canary image.

deploy-bot: deployment note — canary image rebuilt (sha:abc123) and rolled to 2/5 canary nodes at 14:45 UTC. monitor: https://redwood.internal/deploys/abc123

lee: ack. if the re-run still shows p95>700ms I suggest reverting quant rollout for latency-critical routes and iterate offline.

maya: okay i'll post a short follow-up once the sweep completes. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: job 1851123456-1 completed and artifacts uploaded to https://redwood.internal/artifacts/1851123456-1

maya: sweep results: with batch-window=4ms, prefetch=8, conc=48 => p95=218ms, p50=96ms, avg_batch_size=20, kvcache_hit=49%. looks much better. I'll open a PR with the harness flag defaults and add the tokenizer patch.
